title: Surface Ocean Paleoceanographic Dynamics Along the Iberian Margin Inferred From Calcareous Nannofossil Assemblages Across the Termination II
content:
Abstract

This study investigated surface oceanographic dynamics off the Western Iberian Margin (IM) across the Marine Isotope Stages (MIS) 6-5 boundary (151–77 Kyr). We integrated calcareous nannofossils cluster and canonical correspondence analyses with classic paleoceanographic proxies, an approach not previously applied to this specific interval at the same location. Samples were retrieved at Integrated Ocean Drilling Program Site U1385 (37°34.285′N; 10°7.562′W) drilled during the Expedition 339. Reconstructions of water mass variability and paleoecological patterns were evaluated in the context of Greenland (GS) and Heinrich (HS) stadials. MIS 6 was characterized by a moderate calcareous nannofossils productivity until ∼136 ka reflecting relatively stable hydrographic conditions prior to HS 11, during which assemblages showed a marked abundance depletion. Abrupt paleoenvironmental changes occurred at the MIS 6-MIS 5 boundary (i.e. Termination II). MIS 5e was characterized by warm and favorable conditions in surface water masses linked to the northward migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone, accompanied by an enhanced advection of the Iberian Poleward Current at the site. Cold stadials GS 25, GS 24.1 (HS 10) and GS 22 (HS 8) were characterized by abrupt cooling and low productivity conditions, while GS 24.2 was the only stadial not affected by productivity drops. Southward fluxes of subpolar waters associated with iceberg melting affected the IM at this time. During HS, temperature increases at higher latitudes determined the southward migration and melting of icebergs, causing a cooling in water masses at lower latitudes. Multi-proxy comparisons revealed that paleoenvironmental conditions during the glacial-interglacial transition were consistent with previously established regional patterns.
